title: Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders — Schedule of Deduction Rates, Minimums and Bases
content:
Each kind of Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders carries its own deduction terms: a rate, a minimum per payment, the amount the rate is applied to, the way the order states its amount, the rounding of each deduction, and what (if anything) ends deductions by amount. Those terms stand as follows for all six kinds.

## Schedule

| Kind | Deduction rate | Minimum per payment | Deduction basis (amount the rate is applied to) | How the amount is stated | Rounding of each deduction | What ends deductions by amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding | 10% (0.10) | $0.00 — no minimum | Gross payable, before overpayment offset | By rate | Nearest cent | Nothing (no amount limit) |
| Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding | 3.9% (0.039) | $0.00 — no minimum | Gross payable, before overpayment offset | By rate | Nearest cent | Nothing (no amount limit) |
| Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order | 0 — the order states a fixed weekly amount | $0.00 — no minimum | Net after overpayment offset | Weekly amount stated on the order | Nearest cent | Nothing (no amount limit) |
| Child Support Withholding — Arrears-Only Order | 0 — the order states a fixed weekly amount | $0.00 — no minimum | Net after overpayment offset | Weekly amount stated on the order | Nearest cent | The certified amount |
| SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Household or Agency Error | 10% (0.10) | $10.00 | Net after overpayment offset | Rate with a minimum | Nearest cent | The certified amount |
| SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Intentional Program Violation | 20% (0.20) | $20.00 | Net after overpayment offset | Rate with a minimum | Nearest cent | The certified amount |

## Notes on the columns

1. **Deduction rate.** The share of the deduction basis withheld from each payment, as a decimal (shown also as a percentage). A rate of 0 does not mean that nothing is withheld: it means the order states a fixed weekly amount instead of a rate.
2. **Minimum per payment.** The smallest deduction taken from a payment when the rate yields less. A minimum of $0.00 means no minimum applies.
3. **Deduction basis.** Either the gross payable amount of the payment before any overpayment offset, or the net payable after the overpayment offset.
4. **How the amount is stated.** "By rate" means the deduction follows from the rate alone; "weekly amount" means the order names a fixed amount per week; "rate with a minimum" means the rate applies and the minimum per payment stands as a floor.
5. **Rounding.** Every deduction of every kind is rounded to the nearest cent.
6. **What ends deductions by amount.** For kinds marked "the certified amount", the order states a total to be recovered and deductions end by amount once that total is reached; kinds marked "nothing" have no amount limit.

## Points of reading

- *Which kinds are computed on the payment before the overpayment offset?* Only the two voluntary income tax kinds: Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding and Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding use the gross payable amount. The four agency kinds use the net after the overpayment offset.
- *Which kinds have a minimum per payment?* Only the two SNAP Overissuance Recovery kinds: $10.00 for Household or Agency Error and $20.00 for Intentional Program Violation. The other four kinds show $0.00, meaning no minimum.
- *Which kinds stop by amount?* Child Support Withholding — Arrears-Only Order and both SNAP Overissuance Recovery kinds, each by its certified amount. Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order and both voluntary kinds have no amount limit.
- *Do the two SNAP kinds share one rate?* No. Household or Agency Error carries 10% with a $10.00 minimum; Intentional Program Violation carries 20% with a $20.00 minimum.
